question: First establish a genuinely discriminating fifth-action information-value task, before training the Hybrid again. Does a public-context-conditioned factual probe demonstrably beat equally budgeted fixed/random probes, with held-out sign and context balance and positive paired-cluster uncertainty? This calibrates the TASK only, not the native Hybrid.

design.context: uncertain_action in {0,1}, public before the fifth probe; q sign hidden until its selected physical effect
design.cross_each_group: 2 public uncertain-action contexts x 2 independent hidden q signs, with group-specific unrelated factual B histories
design.known_mathematical_prior: Bayesian comparator knows this hypothesis class, prior equally likely q signs and public context, not hidden true sign

policies.adaptive: fifth action = public uncertain_action; after observing actual selected fifth effect infer q sign for that selected action, choose minimum squared goal error against known safe action
policies.fixed: fifth action0 or action1 regardless of context
policies.random: SHA256 deterministic fifth probe of public panel/group/context only, never hidden q
policies.uninformed: without valid fifth effect, choose the Bayes minimum expected squared loss over equal q-sign prior
policies.same_budget: four factual early A effects, exactly one selected factual fifth A effect and identical unrelated B effects for every policy

score.unit: mean first-return squared-goal-error regret vs evaluator-only hindsight optimal action (lower better)
score.bootstrap: paired resampling of 12 groups, two contexts and both q signs retained per sampled cluster

next_neural_gate.compare: native learned dynamics + planner vs native direct action selection vs fully converged GRU/SSM or explicit estimator with same selected factual info and measured total compute
